flags.observation: "So I modify. Modifying is a career." is a short two-line beat with little independent content of its own, mainly bridging Cardiac and Respiratory.
"Prometheus was anatomically correct" compresses a mythological reference into one line; the liver-regeneration joke depends on recognizing the myth.
"the spider usually eats it" introduces an isolated predator image unconnected to the badger-drummer motif used elsewhere for the heart.
The Semmelweis beat narrates history in third person, then beat 23 pivots to the performer's own first-person denial ("we reject the finding") without a signaled transition.
"It was the first Kayfabe." uses wrestling jargon that stands apart stylistically from the medical and historical vocabulary used in the surrounding beats.
The free-will reveal ("five hundred milliseconds before you made it") shifts the piece from body-as-city satire to a meta-statement questioning the narrator's own reliability.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" follows directly after the thematic closing line in beat 31, breaking tonal continuity with an unrelated sign-off phrase.

individuality.observation: Specific named material (Vesalius, Semmelweis, a Libet-style free-will reveal) avoids generic body trivia, though "the first Kayfabe" reads as an imported term not otherwise part of this piece's vocabulary.

outro.observation: "ask him to make his own heart beat" lands as a sharp callback, but the closing "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" shifts register abruptly away from the voice built through the rest of the piece.

performer.observation: A smug, bureaucratic press-secretary voice is sustained through lines like "I already know what they are" and "Of course I did".

standalone.observation: The press-briefing conceit (body run by a city government) is established and explained within the first four beats before any specialized terms appear.

storyBetweenCards.observation: Named items (Heart, Lungs, Liver, Gut) read mostly as a department catalog; the arc lives in the framing (spin, cover-up, reveal) more than in causal links between the cards themselves.

transferable.observation: Organ-specific facts and named historical figures are tightly bound to anatomy; moving this to another topic would require rewriting nearly every department report.

lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

Good morning. Sit down, please. I'll take your questions at the end. I already know what they are.

I speak for the Biological Metropolis. Top floor, corner office, the wrinkly one with the view.

Today's topic: The City Inside has been running the civilization while you were busy with other things.

Population, one. The Citizen: you never once told this city what to do. It never once asked your permission.

Department reports. I read them out loud, because reading out loud is my department.

Cardiac. The Heart: the brain can modify the rate. The brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.

So I modify. Modifying is a career.

Respiratory, my favourite. The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override. Breathe in. See? Mine.

Waste management. The Liver: Prometheus was anatomically correct. It's the only organ that grows back.

Public transport. The Gut: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city. I answer the phone.

Overnight, The Night Shift: sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.

Security briefing. No cameras for this part.

The Immune System: a library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.

Why that matters: DNA Replication: one error per billion letters; you have had cancer, the spider usually eats it.

No spin on this one. Cancer: evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; it is a competitor.

Friendly fire next. Inflammation: the response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.

Autoimmune: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine, pointed the wrong way.

Off the record, between us professionals.

The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. That's not lying. That's coverage.

Historical corrections. We do issue those. Eventually.

Andreas Vesalius looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.

Ignaz Semmelweis saved the mothers. The doctors committed him. He died of the infection.

Our official position has not changed. The Semmelweis Problem: evidence available, implication uncomfortable, we reject the finding.

My predecessor, with respect. The Humoralist: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.

One more item. Somebody leaked a memo. It's about me.

The Brain: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.

You are the press secretary, not the president.

And I just read it to you myself. Of course I did.

The Scorekeeper: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.

Questions? No? Good. I answered them half a second before you asked. The badger never stopped drumming. This briefing is over.

Next time a man at a podium tells you he runs the place, ask him to make his own heart beat.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

styleA: Tight seventies funk at 104 BPM: clavinet riffs, choppy wah guitar, slap bass, crisp dry drums with rim clicks, three-piece horn stabs on the offbeats, short organ swells. One smooth male baritone talk-singer, unhurried and pleased with himself, perfect diction, leaning into pauses. Close-miked dry vocal, punchy analog mix with tape warmth; sudden stops where only bass and kick keep going.
styleB: Big beat at 122 BPM: chopped breakbeat drums, distorted acid bassline, scratched vinyl stabs, sampled brass hits, rising filter sweeps. One deadpan male baritone, clipped and precise, slightly bored, with a thin megaphone filter in the drops. Loud compressed mix, hard cuts to silence before each new section.
